body:
Label corrected: `pm:blocked` → `needs-user-decision`. The `Blocked-by: #9497` line in the body is **stale** — #9497 closed hours ago, so the unlock sweep would have put this card back in the queue as dispatchable, which it is not.

What actually holds it is an input only the maintainer can give. #9497 measured U6 as **not answerable from here**: `changesets/action` is a compiled Action that cannot run outside GitHub Actions, and that repository is outside this session's authorised scope, so its bundled `@changesets/read` could not be read either. The decisive library-level fact *was* measured — after a v3 cut the CLI sees the full stock while a v2-era non-recursive reader sees only the unconsumed residue — but which generation each action version bundles is unknown.

So the question is one of these two, and it is not a technical judgment I can make for you:

- **A** — bring `changesets/action` into this session's repository scope (or paste v1's and v2's reader), and this card answers #9208 properly.
- **B** — dispatch it now for the half that is answerable: read `release.yml`'s pin rationale (#6170), state what v2 would have to preserve, and record an explicit *deferral* on #9208 rather than a decision.

Recommendation unchanged from #9497's: **A**, because B pays for the missing half later, and the failure mode it guards against is the version PR quietly ceasing to refresh mid-window — invisible until a cut is dispatched against a stale number, which is the exact shape of #4898.

Not urgent, and nothing else in the epic waits on it: `release.yml` still pins `@v1` and works, and #9208 is held rather than dangling. This card simply sits in the decision inbox until answered.

Triage note recording maintainer guidance (2026-08-18, live PM chat with the triage seat, session `session_01EUZUjvnLsqwHVkXkTv8TKQ`; verbatim: 「其他接受你的建议」, applying the recommendation delivered for this card).

**Accepted posture: the default answer is DEFER.** The #6170 pin has a recorded rationale; "Dependabot offered v2" is not a reason. The epic side (#9465) produces the evidence per this card's own procedure — what the v1 pin protects, whether v2 changes the `version`/`publish` invocation under v3's exit-1-on-no-op (U6 on #9497), and any new inputs/permissions — and the maintainer nods on the resulting fold-in/defer proposal only if the evidence argues for v2. No maintainer action is due now; the card stays in the inbox as the epic's decision-procedure card. This comment exists so the next Dependabot re-offer meets a recorded default instead of a fresh debate.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**Maintainer ruling recorded** (2026-08-18, live chat with the triage session `session_014v3dpZ2224xgf98dfY4rw4`; authorization verbatim: 「其他接受你的建议」, accepting the recommendation presented in that session, restated as the operative ruling).

**Ruling: delegated to the epic PM.** The fold-in vs defer decision on #9208 (`changesets/action` v1 → v2) is the epic PM's to make from evidence — #9497's U6 reading (delivered; #9497 closed completed 2026-08-18, report on #9465) against `release.yml`'s pinned rationale (#6170) — without a separate maintainer round-trip. Recorded lean: **defer**, unless U6 shows v2 is either required by the v3 toolchain or demonstrably harmless against the pin's rationale; "Dependabot offered" remains insufficient per this card's own text. The human gate stays where it already is structurally: the release.yml migration PR (#9498) is human-merged, so any fold-in passes the maintainer's hands regardless.

**Blocked-by discharged**: #9497 closed completed 06:52Z with the U1–U6 report. Label: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` (epic #9465 subtree — the epic PM sequences it; other seats keep skipping the subtree per `pm:epic`).

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Answered and closing. Maintainer decision on 2026-08-19, verbatim:

> 同意 9208

The decision this card existed to produce: **do not upgrade `changesets/action` to v2.** #9208 is closed with the full reasoning; the short version is that `release.yml`'s v1 pin encodes a safety property — no `publish:` input means `runPublish` is unreachable — that was asserted against **v1's source**, and this repo has already paid once for that property's absence (`rc.3` and `rc.4` minted with no human). No feature of v2 is needed for the one job we use it for, so there was nothing on the other side of the scale.

**The scope question this card was blocked on is moot.** It asked whether `changesets/action` should enter this session's authorised repositories so U6 could be answered. That access is not needed to decline an upgrade nobody needs — it is needed only if and when there is a reason to take one. The requirement is now recorded where it will be read: #9916 puts both re-verification obligations beside the pin in `release.yml` — the `runPublish` reachability property, and (new since the v3 migration) the bundled `@changesets/read` seeing `.changeset/pre/`.

So this closes as **completed**: it produced a decision with evidence and a durable record, which is what a decision card is for. It did not produce the answer to U6, and that is stated rather than papered over — U6 remains unmeasured, by choice, because measuring it costs repository access we do not need today.

Epic #9465 now has one card left: #9500, the RC-window verification, still on hold until the next pre-mode entry.
